title: Session priority and fair-queueing PRD draft
body:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for a feature that gives per-session priority / fair-queueing across the hosted API. Goal is to let customers express session-level importance (e.g., premium user vs background batch) so the runtime can make scheduling, batching, and KV-cache allocation decisions that balance latency SLOs and cost.

Top-level problem statements:
- High-volume customers with mixed workloads lack knobs to protect latency for high-value sessions without overprovisioning dedicated capacity.
- Current per-request routing policies are coarse (region/tier/model). No explicit session prioritization or soft isolation for conversational sessions.
- Need graceful degradation rules when capacity saturated: which sessions should get KV cache hotness, immediate batching, or be delayed?

Goals (MVP):
- Customer can tag sessions with priority: high / normal / low (string label API)
- Serving runtime will expose SLO targets per-priority bucket (configurable defaults: high=100ms p95, normal=300ms p95, low=1s p95)
- Scheduler will implement fair-queueing across sessions with weighted shares where high gets more immediate slots and cache retention
- Metrics & tracing: per-priority latency, qdepth, dropped messages, KV-cache eviction rates per session bucket

Non-goals (MVP):
- No complex ML-based priority scoring yet
- Not implementing per-user monetary billing changes or quota throttles in MVP

User stories (informal):
- As an app developer, I want session.priority = "high" so my live chat agents always get low-latency responses during peak times.
- As a platform engineer, I want telemetry broken down by session-priority so I can validate the policy doesn't starve normal traffic.
- As a customer success rep, I want to suggest conservative defaults for customers migrating from shared to dedicated, to avoid unexpected cost spikes.

Open design questions / tradeoffs:
- API shape: lightweight header (X-Redwood-Session-Priority) vs session metadata in token creation. Header allows ad-hoc tweaks; metadata is safer for audit.
- Enforcement: soft priority (scheduling bias + cache weight) vs hard guarantees (absolute isolation). MVP -> soft.
- Backpressure strategy: queue-and-delay low-priority requests vs immediate rejection with 429 + retry-after. Which leads to better UX?
- How to tie to billing tiers? Allow but keep decoupled in config.

Scheduler notes (rough):
- Maintain separate FIFO queues per session id, with token/bucket scoring. Use deficit round robin with weight multiplier per priority.
- When selecting batch for a GPU worker, prefer pulling from high-priority queues first until a configured high-capacity share is satisfied; then fill with normal/low to maximize throughput and token-efficiency.
- KV-cache retention: keep per-session LRU slots weighted by priority; implement soft TTL extensions for high priority. Eviction logs emitted to metrics.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (experiment): simulate priority weights in staging by tagging a subset of traffic and collecting p95 impacts (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (MVP): API header, scheduler changes, basic per-priority metrics + dashboard, default configs, rollout to beta customers (6-8 weeks).
- Phase 2: advanced controls (priority by route, dynamic weight scaling based on SLO breaches), admin UI, default anti-starvation policies (12+ weeks).

Success metrics / KPIs:
- For beta customers: high-priority p95 improved by >=30% compared to uncontrolled baseline during peak windows.
- No more than 5% increase in cost-per-token for customers using priority (goal: neutral to slight positive).
- Observability: per-priority SLOs available in Console and regression alerts created.

Risks & mitigations:
- Starvation of normal/low traffic -> implement min-share floor in scheduler and configure conservative weights by default.
- Complexity in KV cache bookkeeping -> limit per-session metadata to small footprint, use approximate counters initially.
- Customer misuse (mark everything high) -> add quota for number of concurrent high sessions per account and surface recommendations.

Notes / TODOs (personal):
- Talk to Leo about current batch selection hooks in runtime (blocking or pluggable?).
- Run a quick simulation script to model high/normal/low mixes (target: 80/15/5) and see expected p95 under different weight configs.
- Draft API proposal for review: include header + optional session registry entry; show examples for webhooks and mobile SDK.
- Check legal/AML implications for priority-based throttling (rare but check).

Quick sketch of API examples:
- Header approach: X-Redwood-Session-Priority: high
- Session create: {"session_name": "agent-xxxx", "priority": "high", "metadata": {}}

Stakeholders to ping: product-hosted-api (primary), eng-serving-runtime (scheduler changes), observability (dashboard + metrics), customer-success (beta customers), solutions-eng (onboarding docs).

Final note: keep MVP surgical and easily reversible. If we overbuild billing or hard guarantees early we'll cause ops friction. This doc is just a brain dump — will convert to PRD skeleton after the simulation outcomes.
